title: NTA JEE Main Official Shift PYQ Pack (Section A MCQs + Compulsory Section B Numericals)
markingScheme: +4 Correct / -1 Incorrect (Section A & Compulsory Section B)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.stem: A solid cylinder of mass $M = 4\text{ kg}$ and radius $R = 0.5\text{ m}$ rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 30^\circ$. The magnitude of static friction force acting on the cylinder is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: For pure rolling down an incline, $f_s = \frac{mg\sin\theta}{1 + \frac{MR^2}{I_{\text{cm}}}}$. For a solid cylinder, $I_{\text{cm}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$, so $f_s = \frac{1}{3}mg\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{3}(4)(10)(0.5) = \frac{20}{3}\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.stem: A $6\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ capacitor charged to $20\text{ V}$ is connected in parallel with an uncharged $4\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ capacitor. The loss in electrostatic potential energy during charge redistribution (in $\mu\text{J}$) is:
questions.explanation: Energy loss $\Delta U = \frac{1}{2}\frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}(V_1 - V_2)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\frac{6 \times 4}{6 + 4}(20)^2 = 1.2 \times 400 = 480\text{ }\mu\text{J}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Werner’s Theory, IUPAC, VBT, Crystal Field Theory (CFT) & Isomerism
questions.stem: The spin-only magnetic moment (in BM) of the octahedral complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ is:
questions.explanation: In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is a $3d^5$ ion. Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong-field ligand, it forms a low-spin $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$ configuration with $n = 1$ unpaired electron. Thus $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Indefinite & Definite Integration, King’s Property, Leibniz Rule & Area Under Curves
questions.stem: The value of the definite integral $I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^{2025}x}{\sin^{2025}x + \cos^{2025}x}\,dx$ is:
questions.explanation: Applying King's property $\int_0^a f(x)\,dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, we get $2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies I = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
